point_192.title: Approval Matrix for Purchasing
point_192.cite: POL-APR-002 v2.0, § Approval Matrix for Purchasing

q605.question: What is a purchase executive's approval limit?
q605.reference_answer: £250,000 gross under approval matrix v3.0 (April 2026). The superseded v2.0 (2024) and the 2024 induction deck say £200,000; the 2016 intranet said £150,000 on net value.

[Approval limits (2016) - NBC Intranet]
[Approval limits (2016)]
Approval limits (2016)
 Role | Limit
 Purchase executive | £150,000
 Senior buyer | £300,000
 Purchase manager | £600,000
 Plant head | £2,000,000
 Limits are on the net value before VAT.

[Approval Matrix for Purchasing · POL-APR-002 · v3.0 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Approval Matrix for Purchasing › 3. The limits]
3. The limits
3.1 Each role's approval limit, gross including VAT:
Role code | Role | Limit (gross incl. VAT)
PUR-EXEC | Purchase executive | £250,000
PUR-SR | Senior buyer | £500,000
PUR-MGR | Purchase manager | £1,000,000
PLANT-HEAD | Plant head | £5,000,000
STORES | Stores | no approval authority
3.2 A document within the raiser's own limit is approved when it is submitted. Ledgerline records the
raiser as the approver.
3.3 A document above the raiser's limit goes to the raiser's manager. If the manager's limit does not
cover it, it goes on up the line to the first person whose limit does.
3.4 Above £5,000,000 the order needs the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline.

[Ledgerline ERP 7.0 User Manual: Purchasing · MAN-PUR-70 · v7.0 · effective 2015-03-02 · SUPERSEDED / old copy]
[Ledgerline ERP 7.0 User Manual: Purchasing › 17. Messages › 17. Messages › Practical Tips]
• If a genuine change in supplier location has occurred, notify the accounts department to update the
master record before attempting to complete the purchase order.
• Ensure all line items on multi-line purchase orders share tax codes that point to the same underlying
region before submitting the order for authorisation.
23. Approval limits
23.1 Approval limits are set on each role.
Purpose of approval limits
Approval limits ensure that commitments to suppliers are made only by staff with the appropriate
financial authority. In Ledgerline ERP, these controls operate automatically at the point of order entry
and commitment, preventing purchase orders from progressing to print or transmission until the
necessary sign-off has taken place. This protects the company from unauthorised expenditure and
preserves budgetary control across the Manchester works and the Leeds unit.

[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.

5. Examples
5.1 Emma Clarke (purchase executive) raises an order for 2,000 battery packs at £119.00: basic
£238,000, VAT 20% £47,600, gross £285,600. The gross is above her £250,000 limit, so the order goes
to her manager, Daniel Okafor (purchase manager, limit £1,000,000), for approval.

£1,200,000 gross raised by anyone in purchasing goes to the plant head, Henrik Weber.
6. Review
6.1 The plant head reviews this matrix every April, and when the organisation changes.

[Approval limits (2016) - NBC Intranet]
[Approval limits (2016) › Approval limits (2016)]
Approval limits (2016)
 All purchase orders, stock requisitions, and capital commitments raised across the Manchester factory and the Leeds unit must comply with the company authorisation tiers. Staff are reminded that all limits apply strictly to the net value before VAT. Value added tax must not be included when determining which band of authority an order falls under, but the tax portion must still be entered correctly for accounting purposes.
 Orders must not be artificially split into multiple smaller orders to circumvent approval thresholds. System audits run regularly from the finance office, and any attempt to bypass controls by raising parallel requisitions against the same supplier account will be flagged. Where an ongoing service or regular intake of cycle components requires multiple deliveries, the total anticipated commitment over the entire order period governs the level of authorisation needed.

[Approval Matrix for Purchasing · POL-APR-002 · v3.0 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Approval Matrix for Purchasing › 3. The limits]
3.4 Above £5,000,000 the order needs the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline.
Ledgerline shows ERR-APR-0009 (no approver found) for such a document; the plant head's office
then records the MD's approval.

[Approval limits (2016) - NBC Intranet]
[Approval limits (2016)]
Approval limits (2016)
 Role | Limit
 Purchase executive | £150,000
 Senior buyer | £300,000
 Purchase manager | £600,000
 Plant head | £2,000,000
 Limits are on the net value before VAT.

[Approval Matrix for Purchasing · POL-APR-002 · v3.0 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Approval Matrix for Purchasing › 3. The limits]
3. The limits
3.1 Each role's approval limit, gross including VAT:
Role code | Role | Limit (gross incl. VAT)
PUR-EXEC | Purchase executive | £250,000
PUR-SR | Senior buyer | £500,000
PUR-MGR | Purchase manager | £1,000,000
PLANT-HEAD | Plant head | £5,000,000
STORES | Stores | no approval authority
3.2 A document within the raiser's own limit is approved when it is submitted. Ledgerline records the
raiser as the approver.
3.3 A document above the raiser's limit goes to the raiser's manager. If the manager's limit does not
cover it, it goes on up the line to the first person whose limit does.
3.4 Above £5,000,000 the order needs the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline.

[Approval Matrix for Purchasing · POL-APR-002 · v3.0 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Approval Matrix for Purchasing › 5. Examples]
5. Examples
5.1 Emma Clarke (purchase executive) raises an order for 2,000 battery packs at £119.00: basic
£238,000, VAT 20% £47,600, gross £285,600. The gross is above her £250,000 limit, so the order goes
to her manager, Daniel Okafor (purchase manager, limit £1,000,000), for approval.
5.2 The same order at basic value alone (£238,000) would look within her limit. That is why limits are
measured on the gross value (§2.1).
5.3 An order of £720,000 gross raised by the senior buyer goes to the purchase manager. An order of
£1,200,000 gross raised by anyone in purchasing goes to the plant head, Henrik Weber.
6. Review
6.1 The plant head reviews this matrix every April, and when the organisation changes.
